originalTitle: US stocks: US market ends mixed as investors focus on tech earnings
simplifiedContent: The US stock market had a mixed day, meaning some stocks went up and some went down. Investors are waiting to see how big tech companies like Microsoft and Apple did financially, which will be announced this week. They're also worried that interest rates might go up, which could affect the market. Additionally, oil prices dropped after President Trump talked about possibly making peace with Iran. The market is also waiting to hear what the Federal Reserve decides about interest rates on Wednesday, which could impact the market's direction.

originalTitle: SpaceX at $100 would imply zero AI value, Morgan Stanley says
simplifiedContent: Morgan Stanley thinks that if SpaceX's stock price falls to $100, it would mean that investors are valuing the company as if its artificial intelligence business is worth nothing. The stock price has already fallen a lot, and some investors think it might fall even more when some shareholders are allowed to sell their stocks next month. Despite this, many analysts still believe that SpaceX has a bright future and will grow, which could make it a good time to invest. This could be an opportunity for investors to buy into the company at a lower price. Analysts are generally positive about SpaceX's prospects, even if some investors are currently negative about technology companies that spend a lot on AI.

originalTitle: Bond investors, unsure about Fed policy outlook, hedge against US rate shock
simplifiedContent: Some investors who buy bonds are getting worried that the Federal Reserve (the central bank of the US) might make big changes to interest rates. As interest rates keep going up, these investors are trying to protect their investments from potential big jumps in rates. They're doing this by buying special financial tools called swaptions, which can help them make money if borrowing costs increase. This is because they think the Federal Reserve might take actions that will surprise many people and cause interest rates to rise quickly. By doing this, investors are trying to prepare for and reduce the potential risks to their bond investments.

originalTitle: Treasuries Rise as Elevated Yields Attract Buyers Before Fed
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: the value of US government bonds (called "Treasuries") went up. This happened because the US stopped attacking Iran, which made oil prices go down. As a result, investors became interested in buying short-term government bonds, which are like very safe investments. This is important because the Federal Reserve (a group that helps control the US economy) is meeting soon, and investors are preparing for that meeting by buying these bonds. The fact that investors are buying these bonds now suggests they think the meeting might be important for the economy.

originalTitle: Wall Street ends mixed as investors focus on tech earnings
simplifiedContent: The US stock market had a mixed day, meaning some stocks went up and others went down. This happened because investors were focusing on the earnings reports of technology companies. The overall performance of the market was uneven, with no clear direction. This matters because technology companies are a big part of the stock market, and their earnings can affect the entire market. Investors are paying close attention to these earnings reports to decide what to do with their money.

originalTitle: Dollar eases as oil prices fall on pause in Middle East conflict
simplifiedContent: The value of the US dollar has gone down a bit because oil prices have fallen. Oil prices dropped because there's been a pause in the conflict in the Middle East. This pause has led to a decrease in oil prices, which in turn has caused the dollar to lose some of its value. This matters because changes in the value of the dollar can affect the US economy and the stock market. The decrease in oil prices and the dollar's value could have an impact on investments and the overall market.
